ev.q: During July–December 2020, 3.1% of adults aged ≥18 years had kidney disease.
The prevalence of kidney disease increased with age, from 1.1% among adults aged 18–44 years
The prevalence of kidney disease increased with age, from 1.1% among adults aged 18–44 years to 3.1% among those aged 45–64 years
Among adults aged ≥65 years, a higher percentage of men had kidney disease (8.3%) compared with women (6.1%).
Estimates are based on household interviews of a sample of the civilian, noninstitutionalized U.S. population.
The figure is a bar chart illustrating the percentage of adults in the United States aged ≥18 years with kidney disease
